claims_about_writeup.why: The write-up (contribution.md) exists and describes build.py as reproducing the capture and vectors end to end, matching this description of deliverables.
The write-up states the identical numbers: 'raises strict pass@10 from 0.1275 (baseline) to 0.7843 (80 of 102 items)'.

message_source_quote: `raman2026-white-bear-steering.md` is exactly this setup: a stance direction at L20-24 (large dose) makes the model write the implied concept into the read position. It uses the cognitive *think/do-not-think* stance from `directed_modulation`.
writeup_source_quote: The starting point was therefore Raman et al. (2026, *white-bear steering*): a stance direction, added at a mid-depth band, can make the layers above the band write the implied concept into the read position, so the *unchanged* lens sees it.
rationale: Both documents name Raman 2026 / white-bear steering explicitly as the starting point, describe the method as building on it rather than reproducing it, and give the same novelty claim: a self-authored visual-imagery stance contrast (picture vs. exclude) that captures the same holding-in-mind direction (cosine 0.85-0.91) but outperforms (0.78 vs 0.69) the paper's think/do-not-think contrast, succeeding where the paper's own second contrast (hold vs mention) failed. The only addition in the message is a brief meta-level remark about why reproduction would score poorly, which does not change the substantive overlap/novelty story told in the write-up.
